clips.title: Temporal 101: Build Your First Durable Application
clips.why: The same idea one level up: a run whose every step is recorded can crash and continue in the same state.
look: The AI agent loop example: the history survives because it was recorded outside the process.
What "durable" means: the work continues after a crash, it does not restart.
clips.after: Temporal keeps the run's steps; the session store keeps the agent's conversation. Together, a dead VM costs minutes, not the ticket.
clips.quote: we pick up exactly where it left off

clips.title: Durable AI Agents Explained: Long Running Agents That Survive Crashes
clips.why: Why an agent whose state lives only in memory loses everything in a crash, and how checkpoint and resume fix it.
look: The problem: state in RAM, and what is lost when the process dies.
Checkpoint and resume: what has to be saved, and when.
clips.after: For our agents the state is the transcript, and the store's append() is the checkpoint, after every batch.

clips.title: When to Use Claude Agent SDK? Agent Harness Explained
clips.why: How the Agent SDK keeps memory between runs, how it handles files, and what compaction does to a long session.
look: The difference between the conversation and the files on disk.
What compaction does when a session gets long, and why a resumed session may look shorter.
clips.after: Nova keeps both: the conversation in the store, the files in checkpoint commits on its branch.

practice.q: Continue the conversation from run 1 in a new query().
practice.hint: The option that loads a session by its ID.
practice.why: resume loads the transcript, and the model continues with everything it knew.

practice.q: Which methods must every session store have?

options.why: The other methods (listSessions, listSessionSummaries, delete, listSubkeys) are optional.
delete is optional; without it, deleting is a no-op, which suits append-only storage like S3.
The SDK calls them append and load.

practice.q: Put a resume on a fresh VM in order.
items: The workflow starts the harness on the new VM with the old session ID
The SDK calls load() on the store before the claude process starts
The entries are written into a temporary config folder
claude starts there and resumes the conversation
New batches are written locally and mirrored to the store with append()
practice.why: load happens once, before the process; from then on every batch is mirrored, so the next machine can resume again.

practice.q: Without listSubkeys() on your store, what does a resume bring back?

options.text: Everything, because subkeys are only used for listing
options.why: Resume itself uses listSubkeys to find helper transcripts.

options.text: Only the main conversation; helper transcripts are not restored
options.why: The docs say that without listSubkeys only the main transcript is materialized.
The main transcript still comes back. Only the helpers' files are missing.

practice.q: Finish the check that notices when the store lost a batch.
practice.hint: The subtype for a failed mirror write.
practice.why: A dropped batch is reported only this way. On a run resumed from the store, it may be the only sign of lost data.
